claims.text: Overall wear resistance of a FeNiCrCoCu thin protective coating is governed by formation of a stable oxide-based tribofilm at the wear interface.
The oxide-based tribofilm acts as a sacrificial layer.
The sacrificial tribofilm protects the underlying coating and substrate.
The initial material is a FeNiCrCoCu thin film on a conventional-metal substrate.
A surface treatment will enhance oxide formation on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Tribofilm formation and stability are the structural mediators of wear resistance.
An oxide-based tribofilm reduces wear of both the coating and substrate.
The surface-treated coating will have better wear resistance than the untreated coating.
The coating wear rate will decrease as temperature increases up to a critical temperature threshold.
The proposed mechanism applies under dry sliding from 20°C to 500°C.
The proposed mechanism applies over loads from 10 N to 100 N.
Substrate material and surface roughness may influence tribofilm formation and stability.
Failure to form a stable tribofilm would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction allows decreasing wear only up to an unspecified critical temperature, implying that wear could increase above that threshold, whereas the falsification rule treats any increase with temperature as falsifying across the stated 20–500°C test range.
